value.title: rs boot announce — seats know who they are again
value.summary: Restore the first-boot announce (announceText) for omp/pi seats under the rs daemon: the daemon reports whether a registration created, re-bound, or merely refreshed a seat row, and the extension derives 'fresh' from that instead of from 'a row exists' (which under rs is always true).

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Since c048ebc2 (2026-08-30, rs cutover) every omp/pi seat boots pij-blind: PijSession.boot injects announceText only when `fresh = registry.read(id)===null || dissolved`, and RustRuntimeSession.boot seeds every rs seat row (never reaped) into that registry BEFORE calling session.boot — so the chosen id always pre-exists (spawn pre-mints it; hand-started seats reuse by pane/process/PIJ_SESSION_ID). Last announce on disk: 2026-08-28. Live proof + mechanism: assets/inputs/diagnosis-2026-09-05.md. Fix: the daemon is the only party that knows whether /v1/register CREATED a row, RE-BOUND an existing id to a new process, or refreshed the same process; it returns that as an additive `binding` field, the TS client passes it through, and PijSession.boot accepts an explicit `fresh` override. Legacy path untouched.

sections.name: goals
value: A spawned omp seat (pij-rs spawn --harness omp --bin omp) receives announceText as its first injected turn.
A hand-started omp seat that reuses its id (same pane / same PIJ_SESSION_ID) still announces on the first session_start of a NEW process.
/new, /fork, reload on a live seat do not announce twice (the original 'exactly one inject at boot' rule survives).
The rs register contract carries the fact additively (`binding: created|rebound|same`), shared by both runtimes through one golden fixture.
One wire frame across harnesses: an omp/pi seat renders an inbound peer message exactly as the daemon frames it for a Claude seat.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Reaping or tombstoning stale rs seat rows (separate roadmap question, plan 095 evidence pointer).

announceText content and the ready-ping protocol (PIJ_ANNOUNCE_TO path) stay unchanged, EXCEPT the one sentence describing the inbound frame, which must describe the frame we actually emit (amended by prime ruling 2026-09-05 when AC8 landed: a boot message documenting the legacy shape teaches every fresh seat to expect the generation it is not on).
Any legacy-daemon behaviour; the legacy TS daemon is stopped for good.

value.claim: spawned omp seat announces on first boot
value.text: LIVE on the rs daemon: `pij-rs spawn --harness omp --bin omp` → the seat's first injected user turn is announceText (`You are pij session <id> …`), captured from the omp session jsonl AND the pane; the spine shows seat.put then the announce inject. CONTROL first on main 46c9314c: same gesture, no announce (paste both).
value.receipt: live-proof.md § AC1: pij-used-tarsier, session 01a06eee-3434-7000-87d9-9f72460f91b7, exactly 1 announce in its own jsonl + pane; control 09:20 no announce, no jsonl

value.claim: hand-started seat with a reused id announces on a new process
value.text: Start omp by hand in a tmux pane whose id already carries an rs seat row (or with PIJ_SESSION_ID set to an existing idle seat): register returns binding=rebound (proc changed) and the announce fires once. Paste register response + session jsonl.
value.receipt: live-proof.md § AC2: pij-troubled-wildebeest re-bound pid 66036(dead)->62414, announce fired once (1 match in new session jsonl)

value.claim: no double announce on /new, /fork or reload
value.text: On a live seat run /new then /reload: register returns binding=same for the reload and exactly one announce exists per NEW pi session id; rust-runtime.test.ts asserts inject(announceText) count per reason.
value.receipt: live-proof.md § AC3 (claim amended by prime): /new + /reload cause NO re-registration (one seat.put, spine seq 7811) hence no second announce; binding=same proven at the wire and by u2 fixture witnesses

value.claim: register contract is additive and shared
value.text: `/v1/register` response gains `binding` (created|rebound|same) with no renamed or removed field; one golden fixture docs/plans/135-rs-boot-announce/assets/contracts/register-response.json is deserialized by a Rust test (crates/daemon) AND parsed by a TS test (core/daemon-wire) — both cite the same file path in their source.
value.receipt: RE-CHECKED on main aa697235 from the COMMITTED tree: git show HEAD:crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs -> pij_testkit::fixtures::read("register-response.json"); git show HEAD:.pi/extensions/pij/adapters/rust-runtime.test.ts -> ../../../../crates/testkit/fixtures/register-response.json. cargo test -p pij-daemon --lib registration_binding 4 passed; vitest rust-runtime.test.ts 18 passed. One file, both suites, both green.
value.note: DOWNGRADED 2026-09-05 by reviewer finding: on merged main the Rust suite still cited the pre-move path (deleted), so the two suites did NOT cite the same file and three daemon tests failed deterministically with NotFound. Cause: a git add that aborted on a deleted path with stderr suppressed, so the fix lived only in the working tree. Fixed in 99269b90 by resolving through pij_testkit::fixtures::read so a future move is a compile error; re-check only after merge and a clean run against the COMMITTED tree.

value.claim: a Claude seat adopted by pane binds to its claude process and receives over the socket, never pointer-drain
value.text: Control first on today's daemon (pointer-drain job observed). After u3: adopt a Claude seat; `pij-rs state` shows the CLAUDE pid (not the pane shell); /tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock exists; a send lands with outcome delivered / origin=injected-to-transport and NO pointer-drain job. Existing rows are not rewritten — a re-adopt fixes a seat.
value.receipt: PROVEN LIVE 2026-09-05 on the composed daemon (live-proof.md AC7): pane %3568 running a shell, claude started inside it — shell 90801, claude child 93017. pij-rs adopt --harness claude recorded proc.pid 93017 (the claude process, not the shell). /tmp/cc-socks/93017.sock exists. A send landed with spine delivery.outcome {"outcome":"delivered","origin":"injected-to-transport"} transport=claude-uds, NO pointer-drain job. First attempt was recorded as an INVALID experiment (claude launched as the pane command, so no shell layer existed and the test could not have failed) and redone. Migration: existing rows are not rewritten; a re-adopt repairs a seat.

value.claim: omp/pi seats render inbound peer messages with the rs frame and still parse the legacy one
value.text: The extension renders `[pij-rs from <id>]` head and `[/pij]` tail, identical to what the daemon frames for Claude seats (crates/core/src/framing.rs RUST_HEAD/TAIL), AND still PARSES the legacy `[pij from <id>] …` head. RED first: a test pinning the old head must fail on the new tree. LIVE: one message to a spawned omp seat captured from its session jsonl showing both head and tail. Rationale: Jordan read the legacy head as the old system — a live-generation message that renders like a dead-generation one is an observability defect at the same altitude as the boot announce.
value.receipt: PROVEN LIVE 2026-09-05 (live-proof.md AC8): message to spawned seat pij-flexible-pelican (session 01a06f11-1b29-7000-9e07-00aad7007425) appears in that seat OWN transcript as "[pij-rs from pij-verbal-silverfish]\nAC8 live frame probe from the PM. No action needed, no reply required.\n[/pij]" — head AND tail, matching crates/core/src/framing.rs. RED first: a canonical-frame witness failed on the pre-fix tree, then the old pinned-head assertions failed as a consequence, and the legacy PARSE test stayed green throughout. Legacy head still parsed; harness/scripts/tmux-claude-topic-scan.py RELAY_RE accepts both heads; announceText now describes the frame we emit.

value.title: Contract, then units, then live proof
value.name: u0 contract → u1 rust ∥ u2 ts → compose + live
value.brief: Freeze the binding vocabulary and golden fixture (u0, PM), fan out u1 (Rust: store insert/rebind detection + register response) and u2 (TS: pass-through + fresh override + RED-first test), compose, then the live spawn proof.
